title: A determinant with two equal columns vanishes
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m\ge0$ an integer and $M=(M_{ik})$ an $m\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. If there are column indices $k\ne l$ with $M_{ik}=M_{il}$ for all $i=1,\dots,m$, then $\det M=0$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant].

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 00AR (section-rings-basic), list item Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet, line 282), stated there without proof; the vanishing of a determinant with a repeated column is a basic property of the determinant used in the proof of the item
